numerical_failure.observed_behavior: On ARM, float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX instead of wrapping to INT64_MIN, so the integer shortcut in _to_datetime_with_unit and sequence_to_td64ns misfires for out-of-bounds float values like float(2**63) because np.float64(2**63) == np.int64(INT64_MAX) evaluates to True on ARM, silently producing incorrect results.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Out-of-bounds float values such as float(2**63) should not take the integer shortcut; they should fall through to the out-of-bounds handling (cast_from_unit_vectorized OOB check and the errors parameter try/except path), which raises OutOfBoundsDatetime or coerces per errors.
trigger_conditions: Running on ARM hardware where float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX instead of wrapping to INT64_MIN as on x86
Input is an out-of-bounds float value such as float(2**63)
Input passes through the integer shortcut in _to_datetime_with_unit (datetimes.py) or sequence_to_td64ns (timedeltas.py)
Timedelta path with non-ns units was also affected (latent bug)

input_output_examples.input: float(2**63) passed through to_datetime/to_timedelta integer shortcut on ARM
input_output_examples.expected_output: out-of-bounds handling: OutOfBoundsDatetime raised when errors='raise', or coerced when errors!='raise'

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: float(2**63) / values at or beyond the int64 upper bound (2**63), OOB relative to int64 range [-(2**63), 2**63)
category_specific_evidence: On ARM, float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX instead of wrapping to INT64_MIN (as on x86), per commit and PR body.
np.float64(2**63) == np.int64(INT64_MAX) evaluates to True on ARM because INT64_MAX rounds up to 2**63 in float64 (PR body).
The integer shortcut in _to_datetime_with_unit and sequence_to_td64ns misfired for OOB float values like float(2**63), silently producing incorrect results (commit message).
Test test_float_to_timedelta_raise_oob_non_ns uses value np.float64(2**63) with unit='s' and expects OutOfBoundsTimedelta with match 'cannot convert input'.

Fix adds guard in_int64_range = (data >= float64(-(2**63))) & (data < float64(2**63)) (or equivalent with np.iinfo(np.int64).min/max) to the shortcut condition: all_round = (mask | (in_int64_range & (data == int_data))).all().
Latent bug in the timedelta path for non-ns units was fixed; the separate OOB pre-check from GH#64619 was replaced.
reproduction_risks: Behavior is platform-dependent: the wrong result only appears on ARM where float-to-int64 saturates; on x86 the overflow wraps to INT64_MIN.
The mathematical violation is the equality check data == int_data passing for values outside the int64 domain, so a reproduction must include an OOB value at 2**63 specifically.
Expected error message match 'cannot convert input' is taken from the test and may differ across versions.
